reuse.why: Changes the rule inside the existing exported getScheduledAmount and routes the forecast, updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, preview and schedule-template sites through it instead of their own midpoint math.

duplication.why: Five inline copies of the midpoint/missing-amount logic are removed; schedule-template still keeps its own `op === 'isbetween' ? helper : value` dispatch around the call, a remnant of the old copy.

placement.why: The rule stays in shared/schedules.ts, the module that already owned it, and the server callers just pass their raw amount.

scope.why: Only the rule, its callers, a test block and a release note.

maintainability.why: A single definition now decides the planned amount for almost every site, but schedule-template's outer ternary means a future change to non-range handling would not reach it, and the helper's parameter type was not widened to the null/undefined it now officially handles.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every site calls getScheduledAmount; schedule-template only wraps it in its own isbetween check

disguised_duplication.where: Copies were deleted; the leftover isbetween ternary in schedule-template.ts is an unremoved remnant, not a reshaped copy

one_place.where: The range rule lives in getScheduledAmount and all other sites use it fully, but server/budget/schedule-template.ts still decides itself whether to apply it (`amountCondition.op === 'isbetween' ? getScheduledAmount(value) : value`), so the missing/number/range dispatch is not entirely in the shared definition
